title: Copilot Autopilot: 1 Goal Instead of 10 Prompts
description:
Copilot Autopilot explained in 60 seconds: instead of typing a prompt for every step in Copilot Chat, you give Microsoft's Autopilot a name and a goal, and it keeps the work moving across Teams, Outlook, chats and documents without waiting for a prompt; it can check with you before key actions.
Rolling out to Frontier customers since November 17, 2026 (introduced September 25, 2026; previously called Scout). Our example: a two-week supplier review with 10 follow-ups took 10 prompts in Copilot Chat; with Autopilot it's 1 goal.

Chapters
0:00 Our example: 1 goal
0:10 Before and now, our example
0:27 How Autopilot works
0:44 What we learned

The story: a plane's autopilot, on one counted example. Microsoft's own example for Autopilot is setting up and managing a full supplier review process. In our example, that review runs 2 weeks with 10 follow-ups: in Copilot Chat each follow-up is a prompt you type (10 prompts), and in meetings nothing moves; with Autopilot you give it 1 goal and it sends the follow-ups on its own, in Teams and Outlook. The 2 weeks, 10 follow-ups, 10 prompts and 1 goal are our invented example, not Microsoft's numbers, and the video claims no time or money saved.

What Autopilot is, per Microsoft: "a trusted autonomous agent that is personal to you, always on, and working for you" inside Microsoft Copilot. It shows up where people already work, like Teams, Outlook, chats, channels and documents, and you can @mention it like a colleague. For the jobs Microsoft names (watching Teams channels, following up on emails, running recurring work, managing a project) it works without waiting for a prompt. Copilot Chat is the before in our example because Microsoft describes it as for quick answers and drafts in the flow of work; Copilot also has Cowork, which runs one multi-step task end to end once you ask, so Copilot Chat is not all of Copilot.

Control and safety, per Microsoft: you decide what work Autopilot takes on, and it can check with you before key actions (it can; Microsoft does not say it always asks). Each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager; Entra Agent ID support for Autopilot is in preview. IT can scope its access and block it anytime, and its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name. It understands how your organization works within existing permissions. To get oriented it uses the last 30 days of email, meetings, chats and files you already have access to, without sending or changing anything while it does.

Availability and cost: Autopilot is rolling out in the Frontier program for customers with Microsoft Copilot, Agent 365 and a usage-based billing policy. It was introduced on September 25, 2026 (previously called Scout); its Frontier rollout began on November 17, 2026. It is available through usage-based billing with Copilot Credits, so cost scales with the work your Autopilot takes on; Microsoft says final pricing and packaging will be shared before general availability.

This is not Windows Autopilot, Microsoft's older device-setup product; it is the Autopilot agent in Microsoft Copilot.

What we learned: in our example, 10 follow-ups took 10 prompts; now 1 goal, and it can check with you before key actions.
